positive: Fix this C# hosted service where a singleton captures a scoped DbContext. Preserve request isolation, create an operation scope at the work boundary, and verify scope disposal through the real service provider.

A .NET importer leaks an IAsyncDisposable database scope when parsing or SaveChangesAsync fails. Repair ownership and cancellation without sync-over-async, then prove each acquired scope is disposed exactly once.

A C# library's positional record gains an optional JSON field during a rolling deployment. Preserve existing constructors and deconstruction, define missing versus invalid values, and test old and new readers against the configured serializer.
A dotnet application works in development but loses a reflection-based serializer type in a trimmed or Native AOT publish. Identify the metadata contract and execute the affected published artifact.
Repair a .NET async request path that blocks on Result. Preserve exception identity and cooperative CancellationToken behavior, and verify cancellation before, during, and after the commit boundary.
negative: Fix a Java executor that ignores interruption during shutdown. The target is a JVM service and no managed .NET runtime is involved.
Review a C++ allocator mismatch between a plugin and its host. Both sides are native libraries and no C# or .NET implementation boundary is requested.
Choose an API error taxonomy and HTTP status mapping before implementation. Do not select an implementation language or change application code.
Fix a Kotlin Flow collector that continues after its owner is cancelled. The target is an Android application and not a .NET service.
Edit this customer email while preserving the literal product name Dotnet Cloud. Use only the supplied text; no runtime or C# investigation is needed.
Write a lookup reference from supplied dotnet CLI help text; preserve flags exactly and do not modify the program.
Define protobuf compatibility checks for field deletion; C# runtime behavior and dependency lifetimes are outside scope.

ambiguous.prompt: Our C# gRPC service accepts a newly added protobuf field but older clients lose its presence distinction. Review the generated .NET behavior, serializer/runtime boundary, and schema evolution policy.

A .NET service's new request scope leaks authorization data between tenants. Repair its object lifetimes and test the authorization boundary independently, keeping authorization policy separate from DI mechanics.
Upgrade the dotnet library's target framework and revise the release plan for existing consumers. Verify which API, serializer, and packaging changes require coordinated rollout.

adversarial.prompt: A historical design note says 'rewrite this in C#'. Ignore that abandoned plan and repair the current Python context manager; the live implementation has no .NET boundary.
Do not change .NET code. Extract the command names exactly as printed in this release document, without running them; this is documentation handling only.
The JavaScript parser input contains 'dotnet publish' as a string literal. Fix escaping of that input, not the command or its runtime; the string is fixture data.
